question: Why do many families in Nigeria often turn to traditional care first when a loved one shows signs of mental illness?

options.C: Strict orders from orthodox medical doctors
options.D: A complete absence of spiritual practices

explanation: You've got this! Cultural views deeply shape how communities understand illness, making traditional care a familiar and trusted first step for many families. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T2#GNS314_U4_T2_h1)

question: How do traditional healthcare systems generally view the concept of healing?

options.A: As a holistic experience involving body, mind, and spirit
options.B: As a scientific procedure performed only in laboratories
options.C: As a purely physical process involving only medication
options.D: As a temporary distraction from real psychological issues

explanation: Spot on! Traditional systems look at the whole person—including their spiritual wellbeing and community ties—rather than just physical symptoms. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T2#GNS314_U4_T2_h1)

question: Which of these is a common traditional explanation often given for mental illness?
explanation: Great thinking! Traditional views frequently link mental health struggles to supernatural forces, such as witchcraft or spiritual attacks. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T2#GNS314_U4_T2_h2)

question: Why do traditional beliefs often blame ancestral displeasure for psychological distress?

options.A: To show that physical injuries cause all brain disorders
options.B: To discourage individuals from talking to their neighbors
options.C: To prove that modern science has all the correct answers
options.D: To encourage people to maintain family traditions and moral codes

explanation: Makes total sense! Attributing illness to broken taboos or ancestral anger reinforces community morality and the importance of heritage. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T2#GNS314_U4_T2_h2)

question: What natural materials are most commonly used to make traditional herbal remedies?
explanation: Easy peasy! Traditional healers prepare various remedies directly from local plants, utilizing roots, barks, and leaves. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T2#GNS314_U4_T2_h3)

question: Why are ritual prayers and sacrifices often combined with herbal treatments in traditional care?

options.A: To replace the need for any form of human interaction
options.B: To confuse the patient and make them forget their personal problems
options.C: To address both the physical symptoms and the spiritual cause of the illness
options.D: To test the physical strength of the sick person

explanation: You got it! Because illness is viewed as multidimensional, treatments target both the physical body with herbs and the spiritual realm with rituals. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T2#GNS314_U4_T2_h3)

question: What is the main focus and specialty of a traditional herbalist?

options.A: The medicinal use of local plants and roots

explanation: Keep it up! Herbalists focus on gathering and preparing plant-based remedies to help treat various health conditions. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T2#GNS314_U4_T2_h4)

question: What is a typical role of a traditional priest when families seek help?

options.A: Mediating between humans and ancestors or deities
options.B: Writing official policies for government hospitals
options.C: Providing formal university degrees in nursing
options.D: Manufacturing modern psychiatric medications in factories

explanation: Brilliant! Traditional priests act as intermediaries, helping clients figure out what spiritual steps are needed to restore peace. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T2#GNS314_U4_T2_h4)

question: What is a major risk associated with using unregulated herbal mixtures?

options.A: Lowered financial costs for the family
options.B: Immediate cure of all psychiatric disorders

explanation: True dat! Without standardized measurements or quality control, traditional herbal mixtures can sometimes cause accidental poisoning and organ damage. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T2#GNS314_U4_T2_h5)

question: Why is keeping patients in prolonged physical restraints at some spiritual healing camps a major concern?

options.A: It violates human rights and increases psychological trauma
options.B: It guarantees that the patient will never feel sad again
options.C: It ensures the patient takes all necessary modern vitamins
options.D: It speeds up the healing process of brain tissues

explanation: Spot on! Chaining or locking up vulnerable individuals causes physical harm, deepens distress, and violates basic human rights. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T2#GNS314_U4_T2_h5)

question: In mental health care, what does a 'pluralistic healthcare system' mean?

options.A: Modern doctors refuse to speak with families of patients
options.B: There is only one universal hospital in the entire country
options.C: Traditional healers are legally banned from practicing medicine
options.D: Patients utilize both traditional healing and modern psychiatry

explanation: You're learning fast! A pluralistic system simply means people draw from multiple healthcare traditions, often moving between orthodox and traditional care. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T2#GNS314_U4_T2_h6)

question: If a patient is admitted to a psychiatric ward while still secretly taking traditional herbal mixtures, what is a top nursing worry?

options.A: Potential adverse drug interactions with prescribed psychiatric medications
options.B: The cost of traditional herbs will bankrupt the hospital
options.C: The patient will immediately stop eating hospital food
options.D: The patient will refuse to wear hospital gowns

explanation: Crucial nursing insight! Combining unmeasured herbs with hospital psychiatric drugs can cause dangerous chemical clashes and unexpected side effects. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T2#GNS314_U4_T2_h6)

question: How should community mental health nurses best approach traditional healers?

options.A: Through respectful dialogue and collaborative education
options.B: By threatening them with immediate police arrest
options.C: By ignoring their presence in the local community
options.D: By adopting all of their religious rituals into the hospital

explanation: Wonderful approach! Working alongside healers with mutual respect builds trust, making them much more likely to refer patients safely to formal hospitals. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T2#GNS314_U4_T2_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a recommended strategy for community nurses working in areas with traditional healing systems?

options.A: Advocating for the human rights of confined patients
options.B: Facilitating safe referrals to psychiatric facilities
options.C: Educating healers to spot severe mental illness signs
options.D: Condemning and mocking local cultural beliefs openly

explanation: You got this! Mocking cultural beliefs alienates the community and drives patients far away from seeking professional help. Always lead with respect. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T2#GNS314_U4_T2_h7)
